The MAX3485 has differential outputs A and B. For RS-485, you connect A and B to the twisted pair. For single-wire, you might connect only A to the wire and leave B biased. But then the driver's B output is not connected to the wire, so the wire only gets A's single-ended signal. The receiver compares A to B. This works if B is biased at mid-supply. Actually MAX3485 is powered from 3.3V. Its driver outputs are differential, but each output swings between 0 and 3.3V. So A can be used as a single-ended signal. The B output is complementary. If B is not connected to the wire, the wire sees A. The receiver compares A to B. B is biased at 1.65V. So when A is high (3.3V), receiver sees 1.65V differential, logic 1. When A is low (0V), receiver sees -1.65V differential, logic 0. That works. So the design is correct for single-wire.
